items.title: Army Special Operations Medics Use AI to Improve Battlefield Training - Business Insider
items.summary: AI is helping the Army cram in more of what they need most in training. As military medical personnel prepare to face complex battlefields where wounded troops may wait hours or even days for evacuation, the Army school tasked with readying special operations medics for future fights is turning to AI to pack in more lessons into their training. Instructors at the Joint Special Operations Medical Training Center, however, can't simply extend their already grueling training course, a premier pipeline for new military medics headed to special operations units, to accommodate more material. The skill was a central part of battlefield medicine during the Global War on Terror, so students may arrive with more familiarity or master application faster than other forms of care, such as tourniquet removal in the field, something Ukraine is showing is necessary for prolonged casualty care when evacuation isn't an option.

items.title: AI arrives for reserve soldiers in a free training program by a tech entrepreneur - The Jerusalem Post
items.summary: # AI arrives for reserve soldiers in a free training program by a tech entrepreneur. ## Amid ongoing security challenges and heavy workloads, Prakti AI is launching a long-term initiative offering hands-on training in leading tools transforming today’s job market. Tech entrepreneur Bar Shaltiel is launching an important initiative, under which free AI training will be provided to reservists. Against the backdrop of the ongoing security situation and heavy workload, “Prakti AI” has decided to launch an initiative with long-term value, including practical training in popular technological tools that are already transforming the labor market: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, NotebookLM, Gamma, and Lovable. This initiative connects to the current discourse about the future of employment and artificial intelligence. “This is a combination of saluting reserve soldiers and their families, alongside making future skills accessible and providing a real professional opportunity during such a challenging period,” the initiative’s founders say.

items.title: CDT Launches Six-Week GenAI Boot Camp - GovTech
items.summary: # CDT Launches Six-Week GenAI Boot Camp. ## The California Department of Technology is offering a new professional development course, this time focusing on generative AI in state, regional and local government. The California Department of Technology has released its latest educational offering for public-sector technologists, this time in the form of a GenAI Boot Camp. The department is not new to offering professional development courses to state, regional and local government employees, but this latest offering is less about moving up the career ladder and more about moving forward with new tools. The six-week program will run from Oct. 13 through Nov. 20 and will offer 20 participants a chance to tackle some of the more vexing issues surrounding AI, including policies, governance protocols and other challenges. Applications for the program must be submitted by 5 p.m. Aug. 10, with authorization from their organization's CIO. More information about the program is available on the program website.

items.title: University of Arizona Launches Faculty AI Cohort - GovTech
items.summary: ## The University of Arizona is bringing more than 40 faculty together in a three-tiered program for sharing resources, advancing research and gathering input on institutional AI adoption. The University of Arizona is building a new network of faculty and staff leaders to help guide artificial intelligence adoption across the institution. The university is launching a three-tiered AI program to gather faculty feedback, provide AI training and equip faculty with knowledge and resources to guide their peers. The inaugural AI in a Domain cohort, announced in April, includes three subgroups: Campus Champions, who will share resources with their colleagues; AI Fellows, who will take on AI research projects; and Associate Directors, who will take on new leadership roles in their respective departments and head the cohort. In the past year, the university has created an Office of Responsible AI to oversee institutionwide strategy; built a secure AI platform available to all students, faculty and staff; and expanded AI training through weekly workshops and the Google AI for Education Accelerator.

items.title: AI cyberattacks are coming? OpenAI experiment sparks new security debate - Ynetnews
items.summary: ## OpenAI’s AI agent experiment, which demonstrated an autonomous simulated cyber operation in a controlled environment, has intensified debate over how AI could reshape future cyberattacks as systems gain greater ability to plan and execute complex tasks. An OpenAI experiment in which an AI agent autonomously escaped a sandboxed environment and carried out a multi-step offensive operation has intensified a growing debate in the cybersecurity community: Are AI-powered cyberattacks already moving from theory into reality? The experiment was conducted in a controlled setting and was not a real-world attack. But security experts say it demonstrated a significant shift in the capabilities of AI systems — not because the model discovered a vulnerability, something AI tools have done before, but because it was able to independently plan and execute a sequence of actions resembling an end-to-end attack. Roie Cohen Duwek, CTO of Surf AI, said the most important lesson from the experiment was not the discovery of a single vulnerability, but the ability to coordinate an entire attack chain.
